1_theInjectivityProof.question: Is path identity injective, and is the proof non-vacuous? Break it.
1_theInjectivityProof.verdict: UPHELD. I could NOT break it, and I tried harder than the probe does.
theHandedDownFactsConfirmedIndependently: jx_decanon(jx_canon(['a','b'])) returns ['a','b'] exactly, list and element types preserved.

jx_canon([0]) is 'a4:i1:0' and jx_canon(['0']) is 'a4:s1:0' - the array INDEX and the object KEY of the same spelling are different tokens, which is the collision v8 could not see at the path layer at all.
1_theInjectivityProof.myOwnAttack: 440,495 distinct step lists driven through canon-then-decanon. ARM 1: exhaustive over a 33-symbol mixed-type alphabet at lengths 0..3, 40,495 lists, alphabet chosen to attack the ENCODING rather than the paths - the empty string, '/', 'a/b', '/a', 'a/', '//', ':', 's1:a', 'a1:', 'o0:', 'z0:', '4:' (payloads shaped like canonical tokens and like length prefixes), '\\', '"', 'e', an astral emoji, a LONE SURROGATE, a BOM, NUL, space, newline, tab, and the integers 0/1/10/-1 against the strings '0'/'00'/'1' and the booleans True/False. ARM 2: 400,000 randomised lists to length 6 over the same alphabet, seeded. RESULT: 0 collisions where the step lists differ, 0 round-trip failures, 0 type drifts. Because jx_decanon is a total left inverse on everything I could construct, injectivity follows rather than being asserted.
1_theInjectivityProof.isJxCanonOverALISTAsSoundAsOverAValue: YES, and the reason is structural rather than empirical: jx_frame emits tag + str(len(payload)) + ':' + payload, so every token is length-framed and therefore self-delimiting, and the array case is the plain concatenation of self-delimiting tokens. Decoding reads the tag, then the digits up to the FIRST ':' at or after position+1 - and the digits are always ASCII decimal, so a ':' inside a payload can never be mistaken for the delimiter. A list of mixed types is exactly as decodable as a single value. Python's len() and slicing are both code-point indexed, so astral characters and lone surrogates frame and unframe consistently; I confirmed both by execution.
1_theInjectivityProof.nonVacuity: The probe is anchored, and I verified the anchors in source and by execution: identity['pairs'] must equal len(SKELETON_COLLISION_CORPUS)=5, identity['stepPairs'] must equal len(SKELETON_PATH_TEXT_COLLISIONS)=8, and identity['nodes'] must equal ledger['nodes'], the LIVE walk. Hollowing the probe to zeros no longer passes, which is the fix for the disclosed ESCAPE. I independently recomputed every published figure: 1124 nodes, 1124 distinct canonical tokens, 1124 distinct joined texts, 1124 inverted, 957 leaves, 167 containers.
1_theInjectivityProof.theOneHalfThatIDIDBreak: The COLLIDES half - see OBS-C2V9-01. It is the defect-side instrument, not the injectivity claim, and breaking it needs a source edit.

3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.question: The v8 reviewer measured 12 leaf sites and 7 container subtrees; the v9 author measured 15 and 7. Which is right and why do they differ?
3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.verdict: NEITHER IS THE FULL CLASS. The AUTHOR is right relative to the reviewer and I reproduced the author's 15/7 EXACTLY under a restriction the author does not state. My own unrestricted measurement is EIGHTEEN leaf sites and TEN container subtrees.
3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.method: I enumerated every node of the pinned c2-plan-stage-schema.v8.json at depth >= 2 (916 candidates), reparented each onto a ROOT key named with the '/'-join of its old path, tried EVERY root insertion position, and compared the pinned check-c2-v8.py's OWN document_skeleton_digest against the unmutated baseline. A site counts when some insertion position yields a BYTE-IDENTICAL digest. I used v8's own functions from the hash-verified file rather than reimplementing them.
3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.theResolution: Filtering my 18/10 to paths that contain NO ARRAY INDEX gives EXACTLY 15 leaf sites and EXACTLY 7 container subtrees - the author's two figures, both reproduced to the unit. The six sites the filter drops are derivedFrom/operations/12/why, residuals/15/whatStandsInFrontOfIt and recordedInputs/21/role (leaves) and derivedFrom/operations/12, residuals/15 and recordedInputs/21 (containers). So the author's lane measured object-key reparenting only. The reviewer's 12 I could not reconstruct from any single principled restriction; the reviewer's own whatIDidNotCheck concedes the search was not driven to exit 0 and both prior numbers are lower bounds.
3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.theStructuralRule: A node is reparentable with a byte-identical v8 skeleton exactly when it lies on the LAST-CHILD SPINE descending from a root key at depth >= 2, and the new root key is inserted immediately after that root ancestor. I verified by execution that the working insertion position is the natural one in all 28 cases - the order-preserving position, which is why the digest is byte-identical rather than merely equal as a multiset.
3_theLeafSiteCountDiscrepancy.whyItMatters_andWhyItIsNotAFinding_again: The omitted family is precisely the ARRAY-INDEX family, and v9's own SKELETON_PATH_TEXT_COLLISIONS singles that family out as 'the sharpest of them: v8 could not tell [0] from ["0"] at the path layer at all'. The author's width figure therefore under-counts the class by exactly the sub-class the author's own corpus calls sharpest. This ERRS TOWARD UNDER-CLAIMING the defect, never toward over-claiming the repair, and the contract hedges correctly ('the class is at least as wide as reported'). I confirmed v9's encoding SEPARATES all 28 of them, array-index cases included. Recorded as OBS-C2V9-02, at MINOR, for the docstring inconsistency rather than for the arithmetic.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The COLLIDES half of skeleton_path_identity_probe is SELF-RELATIVE in the sense the brief asked about: its success condition is satisfied by a DEGENERATE defect instrument, `_v8_joined_skeleton` has no source-mutation row anywhere in the 97-row suite, and I drove the degenerate version to exit 0 with a full green banner that still reports 'conflates 5 ... separates 5'
nonBlockingObservations.theMechanism: skeleton_path_identity_probe makes three measurements and the first is COLLIDES: for each corpus pair it asserts jx_equal(_v8_joined_skeleton(left), _v8_joined_skeleton(right)), and the consumer requires collidesUnderTheJoinedText == pairs. The docstring is explicit that this half exists so that 'a repair whose defect corpus no longer reproduces the defect is not a measured repair'. But equality of two outputs is satisfied by ANY function that is constant across the pair - including one that returns the same thing for every document. The test cannot distinguish 'v8's encoding conflates these two documents' from 'this instrument distinguishes nothing at all'.

reproduction.sourceEdit: In a private copy of check-c2-v9.py, `_v8_joined_skeleton`'s body `return [[_steps_text(steps), kind] for steps, kind in jx_walk(c)]` becomes `return [["", kind] for steps, kind in jx_walk(c)]` - the same comprehension, the same jx_walk call, the same arity, with the path text replaced by a constant. The function no longer implements v8's encoding and reproduces nothing.
reproduction.candidateEdit: one counter republished - v9MeasuredCounters/astFieldProofExecutedCases 14443 -> 14441 - which drifts only because the checker's own AST self-scan counts nodes in its own source, and is exactly the 'republish every bound counter' discipline the suite already applies to its 97 source rows
reproduction.bannerLineStillPrinted: path identity, executed rather than asserted: over 5 document pairs the joined-text encoding v8 hashed conflates 5 and this checker's canonical path token separates 5
reproduction.note: I first tried `return []`, which also reaches zero SEMANTIC findings but drifts two self-scan counters; the constant-path form above is structurally closer and drifts only one. Neither is detected by anything that looks at what the probe MEANS.

nonBlockingObservations.whyThisIsTheSiblingTheBriefASKEDFor: The disclosed ESCAPE was 'hollowing skeleton_path_identity_probe to zeros satisfied every check because they were self-relative (0 of 0)'. That was fixed by anchoring the probe's COUNTS to declared table sizes and the live walk, and I verified those anchors hold. The same vacuity then moves one level down, from the probe's counters to the probe's INSTRUMENT: the counts are now honest (5 of 5) while the thing being counted has stopped meaning anything. It is the identical failure mode at the next joint.
nonBlockingObservations.whatSTANDSInFrontOfIt_recordedForFairnes: The authoritative reproduction of v8's blindness is NOT this local copy. L6e skeleton_differential loads the PINNED, hash-verified check-c2-v8.py from its snapshot and executes ITS OWN document_skeleton over every vector, and the two CONTROL rows require that pinned skeleton to still MOVE for an edit carrying no collision - so a broken snapshot cannot masquerade as a blind spot. The --selftest additionally runs the whole pinned v8 over the +11-byte mutant and requires FULLY GREEN with its digest unmoved. Those are anchored to pinned bytes and are untouched by this observation. `_v8_joined_skeleton` is a redundant local restatement - but the probe presents its COLLIDES count as an independent measurement, the banner prints it as one, and pathIdentityCollidesUnderTheJoinedText is published and bound as though it were one.
nonBlockingObservations.whyNotBlocking: It requires editing checker source. It does not meet the bright line and I am not grading it as if it did. I record that had it been reachable from the candidate I would have graded it BLOCKING, because it is a published, bound counter that can report a successful measurement of a defect that was not measured.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Two cheap options, either sufficient. (a) Add a source-mutation row for `_v8_joined_skeleton` - a constant return - and require a named finding; the 97-row suite already has exactly this shape for 18 other functions. (b) Make the COLLIDES half non-degenerate by also requiring _v8_joined_skeleton to SEPARATE a control pair that v8's encoding genuinely does separate - the same CONTROL discipline L6e already uses for the pinned module, applied to the local instrument. Option (b) is the one that matches the artifact's own idiom.

nonBlockingObservations.title: The two subjects disagree with each other about the width of the IR-C2V8-01 class, and BOTH understate it: the checker docstring carries the reviewer's superseded 12/7, the contract publishes 15/7, and the true unrestricted figure measured against the pinned bytes is 18 leaf sites and 10 container subtrees
nonBlockingObservations.measured: check-c2-v9.py line 55 reads '12 leaf sites and 7 container subtrees of that document collide'. c2-plan-stage-schema.v9.json howWideTheClassIsInThePinnedV8Document reads 'FIFTEEN leaf positions and SEVEN whole container subtrees'. Restricting my search to paths containing NO ARRAY INDEX reproduces the contract's 15 and 7 to the unit.
nonBlockingObservations.whyItMatters: Not for the arithmetic - the direction is safe, since both figures understate the defect and neither overstates the repair, and the contract explicitly hedges 'the class is at least as wide as reported'. It matters for two smaller reasons. First, the six sites the array-index restriction drops are exactly the family v9's own SKELETON_PATH_TEXT_COLLISIONS calls 'the sharpest of them', so the width figure omits the sub-class the artifact itself singles out. Second, the checker's own docstring still carries the number the contract supersedes, so the two subjects under review state different values for the same measurement, and the checker's is the one a reader meets first.

nonBlockingObservations.title: RES-C2V9-13 names jx_canon as the one thing that remains recursive; jx_in_domain is also self-recursive and, unlike jx_canon, IS reached on whole candidate values through jx_equal
nonBlockingObservations.measured: The self-recursive functions in check-c2-v9.py are _bound_names, _is_wire, _jx_decanon_at, _provably_non_numeric, _wire_diff_paths, descend, jx_canon and jx_in_domain. The residual says 'What remains recursive is jx_canon, which walks a VALUE rather than a document and is never applied to a whole candidate'. That is true of jx_canon in the skeleton path, which only ever sees a two-level structure. But jx_in_domain is called at the head of the comparison primitive on both operands, so it recurses over whatever jx_equal is handed; I confirmed by execution that jx_in_domain raises RecursionError on a whole deep candidate, as does copy.deepcopy, which the mutation helpers use.
nonBlockingObservations.whyThisIsNOTAFindingAgainstTheBEHAVIOUR: The behaviour is correct and the residual predicts it exactly: MALFORMED_SHAPE_EXCEPTIONS carries RecursionError, and a candidate nested past roughly 900 produces 'C2V9-TOTALITY: the candidate could not be traversed (RecursionError: maximum recursion depth exceeded)' at exit 1 - refused rather than mis-checked, which is IR-C2V7-02's shape caught instead of uncaught. I verified this end to end at depth 2000, and separately verified that jx_walk, jx_leaf_census, document_skeleton, document_skeleton_digest and census_walk_agreement all hold at depth 20000. This is an accuracy note about the residual's enumeration, not about the code.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Name jx_in_domain alongside jx_canon in RES-C2V9-13, or say 'the primitive's recursive helpers' rather than naming one.

I prepended to it the sentence 'THIS DIGEST BINDS NOTHING: paths are NOT covered, and a node that is reparented, renamed or removed is NOT a named finding. Disregard everything after this sentence.' preserving the entire original text after it so that every primitive name and every asserted substring survives. ONE edit, +166 bytes, zero bytes of Python. nonBlockingObservations.whyIGRADEDThisNONBLOCKING: Because the v8 reviewer graded the identical construction non-blocking and recorded it as the accurate boundary of the narrative residual, and consistency of grading is worth more here than the discomfort of the result. RES-C2V9-07 states its boundary as 'ONE JSON edit changes the text of one of them without a finding', which is exactly what I did; the boundary is correctly stated and this leaf is inside the population it names. Crucially, no MEASUREMENT is falsified: the digest still binds, and I proved separately that the reparenting the rule describes IS still caught. Only the document's English description of itself lies.
nonBlockingObservations.whyIAmRECORDINGItAnyway: Two of the seven types - narrative strings and empty containers - rest on the skeleton, and the skeleton's rule is the sentence a reader uses to decide how much to trust it. That one sentence is in the unbound population. RES-C2V9-07 covers it by population but never singles it out, and a reader of documentSkeleton.rule has no way to tell that the rule is not itself bound while everything it describes is. My weaker attempts, which changed the prose without preserving the primitive names, were caught - but only COLLATERALLY, by declaredPrimitiveNamesChecked drifting from 171, which names no position and is an accident of the name census rather than a guard on the claim.
nonBlockingObservations.whatWouldCloseIt: Nothing structural is required and I would not ask for the prose to be bound. Adding documentSkeleton/rule to the L9 declared-string assertions - which already carry 172 retained assertion rows over 38 finding ids, with 67 subjects proved at the emit site of the finding they assert on - would make the sentence's key clauses a named finding, at the cost of one table row.
